prompt: I'm building virtualization for a feed. Before rendering a row I need its height so I can position rows. My approach: I clone the row node and append the clone to document.body with `position:absolute; visibility:hidden; height:auto`, then read `getBoundingClientRect().height`. It mostly works, but a bunch of rows come back noticeably shorter than they actually render, and rows in our themed "compact density" mode are especially wrong. The real rows live inside a container that uses container queries and CSS custom properties for spacing and font size. What's going wrong, and what should I do instead?

assertions.name: identifies-body-context-loss
assertions.text: Explains that appending the clone to document.body drops the real CSS context — custom properties, ancestor/theme classes (compact density), and container ancestry — so styles revert and the measured height shrinks.

assertions.name: explains-container-query-break
assertions.text: Specifically identifies that container queries resolve against the container ancestor, which is absent or wrong-sized off-body, so queried styles (font-size/spacing) flip and change the height.

assertions.name: recommends-in-place-or-subtree
assertions.text: Recommends measuring in place or via a probe mounted inside the real subtree (or reproducing the container + real width), instead of body-append — e.g. ResizeObserver on the real in-place row.

assertions.name: fixes-inline-size
assertions.text: Notes the measurement must happen at the real inline size (width), since auto height is a function of width.

assertions.name: warns-copy-computed
assertions.text: Warns against copying getComputedStyle values onto the clone as the fix (freezes resolved lengths / kills re-resolution), or otherwise says to replicate ancestors rather than snapshot styles.
